name: Gameface
label: Revelation
lede: Jeff Caudill and Todd Trout kept running into the same two faces at Orange County punk shows, and in 1990 made them a band. Their drummer died in 1994, they carried on as his memorial, and by the late '90s Gameface had become the warmest-sounding band on Revelation.

eras.title: The rhythm section from the pit
eras.text: Gameface grew up on R.E.M., the Descendents and Buffalo Tom, put out 7"s and a first album, and then, in the summer of 1994, lost the drummer who'd been in the band from the start.

years.h: Jeff Caudill and Todd Trout recruit two faces from the O.C. pit
years.p: Paul Martin takes bass and Bob Binckley drums. Both were regulars at the local shows Caudill and Trout kept running into.

years.h: Nemesis Records puts out Gameface's first 7"
years.p: The self-titled debut gets the O.C. power pop tag. The Beach Chair 7" follows in 1992.

years.h: Good is the only album with all four originals
years.p: Gameface's debut full-length comes out on Network Sound.

years.big: We dealt with it by writing songs
years.src: Dying Scene · No Echo · Revelation Records
years.h: Bob Binckley, Gameface's original drummer, dies by suicide
years.p: Binckley died in the summer of 1994. Jeff Caudill, as quoted by No Echo, on how the other three coped; they kept Gameface going in his memory.
years.xp:
Todd Trout told Dying Scene in 2025 that Binckley went to a gas station one afternoon, bought gas, sat down and set himself on fire. Trout remembered it happening around the time of the O.J. Simpson chase.

Jeff Caudill told No Echo the band dealt with it the only way it knew.

eras.title: Three to get ready
eras.text: Gameface returned with a drummer who had a big mohawk and fast hands, and a record whose title track is about the friend they lost. Then Steve Sanderson arrived, Caudill picked up a second guitar, and the songs opened up.

years.h: Three to Get Ready brings Gameface back with Phil Hansen on drums
years.p: Dr. Strange Records puts it out. The title track is about Binckley's death.
years.xp: Caudill and Trout remember Hansen as a lightning-fast drummer with a big mohawk. Dr. Strange's owner, Bill "Doc" Plaster, told the band he'd be part of whatever came next if they wanted to carry on.

years.h: Steve Sanderson takes the drum stool and the songs open up
years.p: Sanderson joins after Three to Get Ready. Caudill says his drumming let Gameface's songwriting expand.

years.cap: Gameface at the New Bedford fest, Massachusetts, March 1996
years.h: Caudill ends up upside down from a basketball rim in New Bedford
years.p: At a Gameface show in New Bedford, Massachusetts, the singer hangs from the hoop, a photo fans still pass around. The next night the band plays CBGB.

years.h: Cupcakes and The Reminder arrive in the same year
years.p: The Cupcakes 7" comes out on Only Souvenir, and Dr. Strange collects Gameface's demos and early songs as The Reminder.

years.h: Caudill adds a second guitar to the singing
years.p: Revelation's bio says it gave Gameface a fuller, warmer sound.
years.xp: By November 1998 Caudill couldn't picture going back: he said he didn't know what the band had been doing all those years without him on second guitar.

eras.title: Revelation, and a bassist out the door
eras.text: On Revelation, Gameface became a touring band: five US tours and one in Europe by the label's count, and two albums that sit between hardcore, emo and plain good rock songs. It ended with a bassist quitting before a record came out and a drummer leaving for a Geffen band.

years.h: Gameface share the Troubadour with Jimmy Eat World and Sense Field
years.p: A month before their Revelation debut, the bill in Los Angeles also has [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]] and [[Sense Field|8d7bf045-1526-404d-b37c-6f49b714d614]].

years.h: Every Last Time is Gameface's first Revelation record
years.p: REV 75, and the first with Steve Sanderson and two guitars. The first vinyl run is just 211 on clear.

years.h: A split 10" with Errortype:11, pressed once
years.p: What's Up Bro? is 330 copies on opaque orange, on Revelation.

years.h: Paul Martin quits before Always On comes out
years.p: Revelation REV 99, Gameface's second album for the label. The bassist leaves after recording it.
years.xp: That left a hole when it came time to promote the record. Guy Julian, who officially joined in May 2001, is the bassist in the Always On music video even though he doesn't play on the album.

years.h: Guy Julian replaces Paul Martin on bass
years.p: The Feels a Lot Better EP comes out on Firefly Recordings the same year.

years.h: Sanderson leaves for Instruction, then signed to Geffen
years.p: He goes before Four to Go comes out on Doghouse Records.

years.h: Four to Go is the last word for a while
years.p: Gameface stop after it. Caudill later said he'd put so much emotional stock in the band that it felt like part of him.

eras.title: Now is what matters now
eras.text: A Revelation birthday party brought Gameface back. The album that followed was written while Jeff Caudill's father was dying, with old friends from Big Drill Car and Sense Field singing on it.

years.h: Revelation's 25th anniversary brings Gameface back for night zero
years.p: Gameface play the Glass House in Pomona, their first show since 2003.
years.xp: Jeff Caudill told the Washed Up Emo podcast in October 2012 that the band had needed the years apart to get used to having each other in their lives again.

q: That's the best and most concise album Gameface has ever done.
years.h: Eleven years on, Now Is What Matters Now
years.p: Equal Vision puts it out. Caudill wrote Come On Down while his father was dying of lung cancer.
years.xp: Frank Daly of [[Big Drill Car|15689186-1537-445b-a659-dbb071416e6c]] and Jon Bunch of [[Sense Field|8d7bf045-1526-404d-b37c-6f49b714d614]] sing on the record. Caudill doesn't hedge about where it ranks.

years.h: Back on Revelation with I Owe You One
years.p: The 7" is REV 179: 330 on black and 545 on opaque yellow.

eras.title: Thirty years on, still writing
eras.text: Three decades after Three to Get Ready, Caudill and Trout were still telling Bob Binckley's story in interviews, and Gameface were still putting out new songs.

years.h: Caudill and Trout look back at Three to Get Ready
years.p: For the album's thirtieth anniversary they sit down with Dying Scene to talk about Binckley and the record Gameface made after losing him.

years.h: All My Friends EP lands on Iodine Recordings
years.p: Two new songs, All My Friends and Men of Stone, written by Caudill for friends going down rabbit holes or facing failing health.
